requirement:
# REQ-2234: The analyzer does not work if SuppressSourceGeneration = true

Source: https://github.com/MessagePack-CSharp/MessagePack-CSharp/issues/2234

#### Bug description

The analyzer does not work if SuppressSourceGeneration = true. This has happened since version 3.1.1. It still worked in 3.1.0.

story.summary: TypeCollector no longer crashes on two kinds of bad contract. When a member's key kind (int vs string) does not match the other members, it now reports MsgPack005 and skips that member (`continue`). When two members share a key, it no longer calls Dictionary.Add a second time, which would throw. These edits are in both member-collection loops. The change also adds analyzer tests for SuppressSourceGeneration types, runtime execution tests, and a README section. Separately, it relaxes the max-depth check in MessagePackSecurity.DepthStep from `>=` to `>`.
story.why: The likely root cause is that duplicate or mixed keys made TypeCollector throw an ArgumentException. That would take down the whole analyzer, which matches the report that the analyzer 'does not work' for SuppressSourceGeneration types. No line in the diff touches the SuppressSourceGeneration code path itself. So the theory that this was the cause is inferred from the tests, not shown in the diff.
touches_beyond_requirement: src/MessagePack/MessagePackSecurity.cs L233: the depth limit changes from `>=` to `>`. This lets deserialization go one level deeper than MaximumObjectGraphDepth. It is unrelated to the analyzer and is a security-relevant behaviour change.
README.md: a new 'Opting out of source generation' docs section. It makes behavioural promises, such as MsgPack012 being reported, that no test checks.
The TypeCollector guards also apply to normal (non-suppressed) [MessagePackObject] types.
story.confidence_overview: Medium that the TypeCollector guards stop the analyzer from crashing on duplicate or mixed keys in the property path; tests target exactly that. Low that this is the whole root cause of REQ-2234, because the suppression path is not visible. The second (field) loop's changes have no direct test. The MessagePackSecurity change is clearly out of scope and weakens an untrusted-input limit.

findings.description: Changing `>=` to `>` lets an object graph go one level deeper than MaximumObjectGraphDepth before InsufficientExecutionStackException is thrown. This weakens a stack-exhaustion defense for untrusted input. It is unrelated to REQ-2234 and is not tested.

If 3.1.1 instead skips suppressed types early somewhere outside this diff, the bug is only partly fixed. Running the new tests against the pre-change code would confirm which is true.

The new `continue` skips all later per-member processing for a member whose key kind is mismatched. That includes the formatter-attribute lookup and member-type validation (e.g. MsgPack003), so other diagnostics on that member can be silently lost.
